oewn-02473085-v.learner: to break something up into parts or shares
examples: But in what proportions it should be divided amongst the latter depended on the will of the parents.
Her heart was divided between concern for her sister and resentment against all others.

oewn-02627934-v.learner: to stand between two things and keep them apart, like a wall
examples: Mr. Darcy was almost as far from her as the table could divide them.

oewn-01559703-v.learner: to force, take, or pull two things apart from each other
examples: what is to divide them?--the upstart pretensions of a young woman without family, connections, or fortune!

oewn-00244010-v.learner: to join things together, or to put them together into one
examples: Elizabeth tried to unite civility and truth in a few short sentences.

oewn-02475258-v.learner: to act together with others, or to come together in a shared aim or belief
examples: Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia
The united efforts of his two unfeeling sisters, and of his overpowering friend

oewn-02628315-v.learner: to be joined to something else, or to become joined or linked to it
examples: Miss Elizabeth Bennet would, in all likelihood, be soon afterwards united to my nephew

oewn-00710809-v.learner: to have something as your aim, or to mean to do it
examples: I propose here to show cause.
She had fully proposed being engaged by Wickham for those very dances

oewn-00876925-v.learner: to put forward an offer or a plan for something
examples: "Have you anything else to propose for my domestic felicity?"
Miss Bingley was then sorry that she had proposed the delay

oewn-00881285-v.learner: to ask someone to marry you
examples: He proposed to her the evening after the ball, and she accepted him at once.

oewn-07370091-n.learner: the event of a living thing dying, or leaving life
examples: he paid her not the smallest attention till her grandfather's death made her mistress of this fortune
The death of your daughter would have been a blessing in comparison of this.

oewn-11464213-n.learner: the lasting end of all life activity in a living thing, or in one part of it
examples: The cold brought on the death of the tissue in his frozen fingers.

oewn-15168236-n.learner: the time at which a life ends, up to which something goes on
examples: She nursed her father faithfully until his death.

oewn-04905614-n.learner: behaviour that is correct, or that suits the occasion
examples: Mr. Darcy, with grave propriety, requested to be allowed the honour of her hand, but in vain.
Miss Darcy... could not have appeared with propriety in a different manner.

connotation.why: measures behaviour against an accepted standard and approves it

oewn-05146223-n.learner: any good quality that deserves to be admired
examples: Miss Bennet eagerly disclaimed all extraordinary merit, and threw back the praise on her sister's warm affection.
construction is not the highest merit, the choicest gift, of the novelist

connotation.why: names a quality as admirable rather than simply naming it

oewn-04814129-n.learner: the state of deserving something, such as help or a reward
examples: Places at the school are given on merit, so the best pupils get in.

oewn-07123904-n.learner: the passing of messages between people by speaking words aloud
examples: "I must think your language too strong in speaking of both," replied Jane
I have not been accustomed to such language as this.

oewn-06293304-n.learner: an ordered system for saying things to others, using sounds or agreed signs
examples: French was the first language she learned after her own.

oewn-05658665-n.learner: the power of the mind that lets people speak
examples: Only human beings have language, and it marks them off from every other animal.

oewn-02610777-v.learner: to have some quality; the linking word set before a describing word or a naming word
examples: she "wished they might be happy."
But to be guarded at such a time is very difficult.

oewn-02622439-v.learner: to be the very same person or thing as the one named
examples: The writer of that unsigned letter must be Mr. Darcy himself.

oewn-02661230-v.learner: to sit in a certain place or take up a certain space
examples: Her gloves must be somewhere in the drawing room.

oewn-00071785-n.learner: something done wrongly through poor judgement, not knowing, or not paying attention
examples: On the first head she could not make a mistake
Wretched, wretched mistake!

oewn-05904330-n.learner: a way of understanding something that is not right
examples: Mr. Darcy related the mistake which had occasioned his intruding on Miss Bennet
"my dear," said Maria, quite shocked at the mistake, "it is not Lady Catherine.

oewn-06782183-n.learner: a piece of something said or written that is wrong
examples: There is a mistake in the third line of your letter, for the date is wrong.

oewn-04682671-n.learner: the way a person or thing appears to others on the outside
examples: To complete the favourable impression, she then told him what Mr. Darcy had voluntarily done for Lydia.

oewn-05945422-n.learner: a sharp picture in the mind that tells you a lot
examples: The first sight of the great house left a lasting impression in her mind.

oewn-05925333-n.learner: an unclear idea that you still trust to some degree
examples: I had an impression that the two of them had met before, though neither of them said so.
